**My reasoning, as this farmer:**

My family has farmed this land for generations. I know Quzhou's soil — it's good flat ground on the North China Plain, and everyone here grows the same two things: winter wheat, then summer maize. That rotation is what makes sense here. The seasons fit it, the machinery rental is available for it, my neighbors do it so I can borrow help and share equipment costs, and the grain station in town buys both crops. I don't have any reason to change what has always worked.

I have about 7 mu of contracted land I farm myself. My son is in the city now, so I do most of the management alone, though I hire day laborers for harvest. I keep 1 mu near the house for garlic and vegetables — that's for eating and selling a little at the village market.

For seeds, I go to the village agri-supply shop and buy whatever improved variety the owner says is selling well this year. I don't read the bags carefully but I trust him — he's been selling seed here for twenty years. For wheat I'll use about 15 jin of seed per mu like always. For maize I'll buy hybrid seed.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer and urea. My neighbor uses about the same amounts I do. I apply a bit extra to be safe — I don't want a poor harvest over trying to save money on fertilizer. My husband taught me these amounts before he passed, and I've used them ever since.

For irrigation, wheat needs water more than maize. I pump from the village groundwater well. Wheat I'll water at overwinter, green-up, jointing, and grain-filling — four times. Maize mostly gets summer rain but I'll pump once if it looks dry in July.

I use rotary tillage before wheat planting. For maize I plant directly into the wheat stubble with the seeder I rent — no need to till again.
